stages.name: Socially engineered clipboard execution
observables: PowerShell command copied to clipboard and pasted by user
Terminal output: I am not a robot - Cloudflare ID: f47f2a8c21c9df4e

stages.name: Steganographic payload retrieval
observables: POST requests to attacker domains for PNG files
Decoding RGBA pixel data to reconstruct executables and DLLs

stages.name: Active Directory and infrastructure discovery
observables: Ping sweeps of dc, sql, db, backup, gateway, and mail servers

stages.name: File-based C2 command loop
observables: PowerShell file-watch loop on local text file
Command results written to output text file

stages.name: Reverse WebSocket SOCKS tunnel
observables: Encrypted WebSocket channel for TCP proxy access

scenario.summary: The TerminalFix campaign utilizes fake Cloudflare CAPTCHA prompts to trick users into executing PowerShell scripts that download and sideload a malicious DLL. The intrusion leverages steganography within PNG files to deliver a second-stage payload, establishes persistent network access via Registry Run keys and scheduled tasks, and deploys a Python-based reverse tunnel for internal network proxying and reconnaissance.

meta.rationale: Scoping focuses on Windows endpoints specifically executing binaries from deep ProgramData paths, as this is the standard staging location for TerminalFix implants. Widen the search if the campaign is observed using other user-writable paths like AppData.
meta.hypothesis: Adversaries are maintaining access via redundant persistence in ProgramData subdirectories and using a PowerShell-based file-watch loop for asynchronous command execution.

blind_spots.risk: Without script block logging, we see the persistence and the presence of the loop, but not the contents of the commands being executed via Invoke-Expression.
blind_spots.question: What specific commands were executed within the asynchronous loop?
blind_spots.requires: hb_script_activity with full block logging (PowerShell v5+)
blind_spots.remediation: Enable Group Policy for PowerShell Script Block Logging and Module Logging.

blind_spots.risk: Snapshots show existing keys but not the timeframe of creation, making it difficult to correlate persistence setup with the initial sideloading event.
blind_spots.question: When was the persistence established and what was the parent process?
blind_spots.requires: hb_registry_activity in log mode (Sysmon Event ID 12/13/14)
blind_spots.remediation: Deploy Sysmon registry monitoring for Run keys in both HKCU and HKLM hives.

hunt.name: TerminalFix: Persistent Command Loops
hunt.description: This hunt targets the persistence and command-and-control stages of the TerminalFix campaign. It investigates the specific redundant persistence markers (Registry Run keys and Scheduled Tasks) used to maintain the LockScreenContentServer implant, specifically looking for execution from non-standard subdirectories within ProgramData. Additionally, it examines PowerShell script activity for patterns matching an asynchronous file-watch command loop, which allows attackers to execute arbitrary code by simply writing to a local text file. Correlation between these persistence mechanisms and automated script behavior identifies hosts functioning as durable network beachheads.
